commits.message:
Release nonlocal router replay target backing storage (#10369)

Copy local router-replay targets so backward recomputation releases
nonlocal backing storage. Keep shared storage when a rank owns the
complete tensor.

Four CPU regression cases check unchanged values and retained storage
for packed/unpacked batches and single-row tensor-parallel slices. They
pass with the fix and fail on the previous implementation. Run them in
the SkyRL CPU CI lane.

Broader replay-suite restoration is in #10632. Ported from [SkyRL
#1031](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1031), source
revision `47d6da95c94fc67ad31cb89678e6bab6e0b67b63`.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finestore] Track row versions and recover expired caches (#10553)

Record original row-commit ranges in shard metadata. Exact primary-key
and blob-descriptor lookups visit candidates by descending maximum row
commit and skip older payloads once no unread shard can supersede a
key's winning row. Table point lookups still read candidate schemas;
descriptor lookups can skip older files entirely.

Recover PersistentKvCache after shard expiry by advancing a cache
history floor to the greatest row-commit upper bound of the missing
files. Reads apply the floor to their local snapshot, ignoring
descriptor and chunk rows committed at or below the floor so superseded
values cannot reappear. Newer entries remain usable, including rows
sharing a shard with older history. The next write persists the floor in
the manifest and removes missing or wholly invalidated shard references,
preserving shards added concurrently by other writers. Compaction
removes invalidated rows from mixed shards.

During writes, refresh live shards and schemas older than half the
lifetime indicated by the cache root's ttl=Nd path segment (N days).
Server-side copies on S3 and GCS reset object age to prevent lifecycle
expiry. Check before the first write, then at most daily or once per
quarter TTL for shorter lifetimes. Reads that encounter missing shards
or schemas request another check on the next write.

Recovery applies to disposable key/value caches. Ordinary archives
continue raising errors for missing committed data. Recovered caches
declare the required cache-history-floor-v1 feature so older readers
reject them.

Namespace every `PersistentKvCache` archive under `<cache-root>/v2`,
including roots resolved by `for_prefix`. The cache adds the version
internally and `location()` returns the versioned archive path. New
binaries use a separate manifest so recovery cannot make the old shared
cache unreadable to older binaries. Versioned caches start empty and
fill as callers regenerate missing values.

Incident record: [expired Cutlass cache
shards](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/847).

Part of #9206.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
Keep Iris startup waits outside the default executor (#10679)

Iris sandbox startup awaits `asyncio.sleep(2)` between readiness polls.
Submission, each status read of the job's single task, and the workdir
`mkdir` run in the default executor; no thread is held while waiting. A
failed or cancelled wait closes the machine. `shellbox-unit` installs
the locked `iris` extra so the Iris adapter tests run in CI.

Root cause: on `main`, `create` runs submission and the readiness loop,
with its blocking `time.sleep(2)`, as one `asyncio.to_thread` call, so
every pending startup holds an executor thread that commands and grading
need.

One matched real RNO 64-trajectory pair (`atqamar-sbc-rno-h64-base-a1`
on `2cae063c8771`, `atqamar-sbc-rno-h64-async-a1` on `8e4c8102511b`):
startup executor-thread-seconds 878 → 79 (−91%), whole-wave wall time
26.9 → 22.8 s (−15%), tool p50 883 vs 871 ms (no latency change
claimed).

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[rl] Group online EAGLE windows by prompt, not trajectory (#10659)

Online EAGLE now groups capture windows by prompt on both request paths.
`request_id_for_session` turns a rollout session id `<prompt
uid>_<repetition>` into a request id carrying the prompt's digest (any
other session id is its own group); the token-in path uses it as the
vLLM request id and the chat-completions path sends it as
`x-request-id`, which vLLM names `chatcmpl-<id>`, so
`request_group_from_id` strips that prefix. All samples of one prompt
now share a group, which makes the per-prompt sequence cap and the
prompt-disjoint holdout work as intended. Routing still uses the full
session id.

Both helpers live in `inference_engines/base.py` so the chat client does
not import the torch-based EAGLE trainer. Checked against the real
helpers: two repetitions of `task_a` (including one through the
`chatcmpl-` prefix) map to one group, `task_b` to another, and
`account_a`/`account_b` stay separate;
`cloud/iris/tests/test_assistant_prefix_harness.py` passes (9).

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[rl] Raise SkyRL rollout concurrency to the in-flight group cap (#10402)

Each SkyRL rollout worker runs up to 1,024 trajectories at once, so the
in-flight group cap and the staleness limit set rollout concurrency. An
Iris launch that leaves `trainer.rollout_buffer.max_in_flight` null sets
it to 1.5 × `train_batch_size` groups, rounded up, so half of the next
batch generates while the current one finishes. In a Harbor run the cap
is at most `n_concurrent_trials` / `n_samples_per_prompt`.
`experiments.post_training.async_rl` gets 192. Evaluation runs at most
as many Harbor trials per worker as training.

With `batch_policy: rolling`, a prompt whose group misses the staleness
limit is regenerated at most `trainer.rollout_buffer.max_stale_retries`
times in a row (default 1), then waits for the prompt order to draw it
again; `async/stale_retries_exhausted` counts such prompts.

Snowball 67B-A2B single-turn math through `async_rl` on 40 H100 in
cw-rno2a (32 trainer GPUs, one vLLM engine at DP8/EP8), 128 prompts × 4
trajectories per step, no evaluation; main and this change launched
together. Medians over steps 2–19 (`default`) and 2–13 (`on_policy`).

| | `--preset default`, staleness 4 | `--preset on_policy`, staleness 0
|
|---|---|---|
| step time | 42.8 s → 27.0 s | 106.4 s → 95.4 s |
| trainer wait for generation | 16.9 s → 0.1 s | 80.6 s → 70.4 s |
| vLLM running requests per GPU | 15 → 48 | 7 → 8 |
| generated tokens/s per vLLM GPU | 1,130 → 2,987 | 667 → 705 |
| trained response tokens/s | 8,894 → 13,839 | 3,731 → 4,468 |
| KV cache use, per-step peak | 4.5% → 13.4% | 3.2% → 4.2% |
| groups discarded as stale per step (of 128) | 0 → 25 | 0 → 0 |

On `default`, mean trained-group staleness rises from 2.06 to 2.74. A
repeat with jobs started 32 minutes apart took 40.1 s per step on main
and 26.9 s, with 21 stale groups, on this change. On `on_policy` the
gain is within the step-time standard deviation (13 s and 15 s). No step
used more than 15.9% of the KV cache; the vLLM waiting queue stayed
empty.

Not run with this change: agentic multi-turn and Harbor tasks, in-run
evaluation, Qwen, CatCount and the MOPD recipes. With this change those
recipes run up to 512 trajectories at once (CatCount canary), 256 and
4,096 (curriculum Qwen arms), and 192 and 384 (MOPD 32k and its async
smoke, one Daytona sandbox per SWE trajectory). The MOPD 32k recipe uses
512 Harbor trials, keeping its Harbor bound (128 groups) above its batch
of 48, and the default `generator.max_num_seqs` (1,024). Daytona and
local task sandboxes have no limit of their own, so in training they run
the trajectory counts above and in evaluation up to 1,024 at once.

Iris jobs (user atqamar)
`users-ahmad-checkpoints-async-rl-snowball-{default-set-06e87ec2,on_policy-set-2cf146b4}-<arm>-2026.09.18-*`,
each running the listed commit plus a run-only commit that sets the job
name and cluster. Default: `ccab1-control` (main 3bf0d7a1be), `ccab1-pr`
(b447962634); repeat `ccab3-control` (main 57e6418017),
`ccab4-persample` (3438434b21, each trajectory placed on a vLLM rank by
its own session id, as on main and in this change). On-policy:
`ccab1-control` (main 3bf0d7a1be), `ccab2-pr-norouting` (7a3ab8329f).

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[harbor] Preserve synchronous tokenization failures (#10630)

Retry transient `/tokenize` failures during Terminus context recovery
and wrap exhausted failures in `ContextManagementInfrastructureError`.
The synchronous path currently hides the HTTP error and tries a local
tokenizer, whose `ValueError` causes Marin to reject the whole eval as
an unclassified failure.

Keep local fallback for endpoints that return 404. Completes the
synchronous path left unchanged by #10584.
